questions.question: The sum of the ages of a mother, daughter and son is 96 years. What will be the sum of their ages after 5 years?
questions.solution:
The sum of the ages of a mother, daughter and son is 96 years.

Mother + Daughter + Son = 96

Sum of their ages after 5 years = 96 + 5 × 3

= 96 + 15

= 111

Hence, ‘**111**’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: A total of 1012 candies are to be distributed among Virat, Ketan and Rohan in the ratio of 6 : 9 : 8, respectively. How many candies will Rohan get?
questions.solution:
Total number of candies = 1012

Distributed among Virat, Ketan and Rohan respectively = 6 : 9 : 8

Let number of candies taken by Virat = 6x, Number of candies taken by Ketan = 9x and number of candies taken by Rohan = 8x

6x + 9x + 8x = 1012

23x = 1012

x = 44

Number of candies taken by Rohan = 8 × 44 = 352

Hence, **"option 2"** is the correct answer.

questions.question: There are three books coded as A, B and C. The price of book A is twice the price of book B and one-third the price of book C. If book C costs Rs. 84, then what are the costs of book A and book B, respectively?
questions.solution:
Given:

Three books coded as A, B and C.

1) The price of book A is twice the price of book B

=> A = 2B → eq. 1

2) The price of book A is one-third the price of book C

=> A = 1/3 C → eq. 2

3) Book C costs Rs. 84

Put the value in eq. 2

=> A = 1/3 × 84

**=> A = 28**

Put the value of A in eq 1;

=> A = 2B

=> 28 = 2B

=> B = 28 ÷ 2

**=> B = 14**

Hence, the costs of book A and book B, respectively **“****Rs. 28 and Rs. 14”.**

questions.question: Ranjan in his ODI Cricket career, scored 15 runs on an average in 10 matches. If he scored 14 runs on an average in the first 4 matches and 12 runs on an average in the last 4 matches, then find the average of the runs scored by him in the remaining 2 matches.
questions.solution:
• Average runs in total 10 matches = 15

∴ sum of runs in total 10 matches = 15 × 10 = 150. 

 
• Average runs in first 4 matches = 14

∴ sum of runs in first 4 matches = 14 × 4 = 56. 

 
• Average runs in last 4 matches = 12

∴ sum of runs in last 4 matches = 12 × 4 = 48. 

 
• Sum of runs in the remaining 2 matches = total runs in 10 matches - (sum of runs in first 4 matches + sum of runs in last 4 matches)

∴ sum of runs in remaining 2 matches = 150 - (56 + 48) = 150 - 104 = 46.​

⇒ average of runs in remaining 2 matches = 46 ÷ 2 = 23

Hence, the correct answer is "23".

questions.question: Two numbers, A and B, are such that the sum of 3% of A and 6% of B is four-fifth of the sum of 4% of A and 6% of B. Find the ratio of A + B and A - B?
questions.solution:
The logic follows here is :-

Given, sum of 3% of A and 6% of B is four-fifth of the sum of 4% of A and 6% of B.

⇒ 3/100 × A + 6/100 × B = 4/5 (4/100 × A + 6/100 × B)

⇒ 3A + 6B = 4/5 (4A + 6B)

⇒ 5 (3A + 6B) = 4 (4A + 6B)

⇒ 15A + 30B = 16A + 24B

⇒ 6B = A

⇒ B/A = 1/6

∴ A = 6 and B = 1

⇒ A + B = 6 + 1 = 7

⇒ A - B = 6 - 1 = 5

Ratio of A + B and A - B is :

A + B / A - B = 7 / 5

A + B : A - B = 7 : 5

Thus, the correct answer is **"7 : 5".**

questions.question: A pipe can fill a leak - proof tank completely in 24 hours. A leakage at the midpoint of same size tank empties half the tank in 36 hours. How much time will it take to fill this tank with the given pipe?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

Time taken by inlet pipe to fill a tank = 24 hours 

Time taken by leakage to empty half tank = 36 hours

Time taken by leakage to empty full tank = 72 hours

**Concept used:**

Let capacity of tank is the LCM of time taken by inlet & leakage to fill and empty the whole tank.

**Solution:**

Capacity of tank = LCM of (24, 72)

Capacity of tank = 72 Units

Efficiency of inlet pipe = +72 /24 = + 3 units / hr

Efficiency of outlet (leakage) = -72/72 = -1 Unit/hr

Time taken by inlet pipe & leakage to fill half the tank = 36over (3 - 1) = 18 hrs

Time taken by inlet pipe to fill next half of the tank = 36over 3 = 12 hrs

Total time taken to fill the whole tank = 18 + 12

Total time taken to fill the whole tank = 30 hrs

Hence, **30 hours **is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/11e549cb45ac78aca065082aa5a940b1d6506603cfff2fd1300a22049ad93dc6.png] 

Leak at the middle so the effect of Leak always on the Half Tank. 

The bottom of tank with water is filled without any leakage because leak point is at middle of tank and leakage occurs while filling upper half of the tank only.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__**

If the leak is in the **midpoint of the base of tank**,

The pipe fills 1/24 of the tank in one hour.

The leak empties (1/2)/36 or 1/72 of the tank in 1 hour.

so total water filled in one hour = 1/24 - 1/72 = 2/72 = 1/36.

So the tank gets filled in 36 hours

**Actual Question solution by another method.**

If the leak is in the **midpoint of the wall of tank**,

Pipe takes 1/12 of tank in one hour

Leak empties 1/36 of water in 1 hour

So total water filled in one hour = 1/12 - 1/36 = 1/18

So the second half of the tank gets filled in 18 hours and the first half gets filled in 12 hours.

Total time taken is 12 + 18 = 30 hours

**Note:** Also **30 hours** is the answer given by the Official answer key of CHSL.

questions.question: 2 train tickets from Mohali to Delhi and 3 tickets from Mohali to Jammu cost ₹800. But 3 tickets from Mohali to Delhi and 2 tickets from Mohali to Jammu cost ₹700. What are the ticket prices for Delhi and Jammu, respectively, from Mohali?
questions.solution:
Let tickets from Mohali to Delhi = x

Tickets from Mohali to Jammu = y

Given that:-

2x + 3y = 800 .................(I)

3x + 2y = 700 ................(II)

We multiply 3 in equation (I) and multiply 2 in equation (II) we get:-

6x + 9y = 2400

6x + 4y = 1400, Now solve both equations, we get:-

y = ₹200 (tickets price from Mohali to Jammu)

x = ₹100 (tickets price from Mohali to Delhi) 

Hence, **"option 1"** is the correct answer.

questions.question: Train A, which runs at a speed of 90 km/h, starts from Station Y at 8 a.m. Train B, which runs at a speed of 120 km/h, starts from Station Y on the same route at 8.10 a.m.. If Train B catches up with Train A at 8.40 a.m. at Station Z, then what is the distance between Stations Y and Z?
questions.solution:
Given:

**Train A:**

Speed = 90 km/h

Time at station Y = 8 a.m.

**Train B:**

Speed = 120 km/h

Time at station Y = 8.10 a.m.

Time at station Z = 8.40 a.m.

Total time taken from station Y to Z = 8.10 to 8.40 = 30 min = 0.5 hours

We know that,

**=> Speed = Distance / Time**

=> Speed of train B = (Distance from station Y to Z) / (Time taken from station Y to Z)

=> 120 = (Distance from station Y to Z) / 0.5

=> 120 × 0.5 = Distance from station Y to Z

=> Distance from station Y to Z = 120 × 0.5 = 60 km

Hence, distance between Stations Y and Z is **“60 km”**.

questions.question: Rohit is three times the age of his son Rishabh. Five years ago, he was four times older than Rishabh. What is Rohit’s age at present?
questions.solution:
Given: Rohit is three times the age of his son Rishabh. Five years ago, he was four times older than Rishabh.

Let the age of Rohit be 'A' and that of his son Rishabh's be 'B'.

Then, according to the question,

A = 3B, implies B = A/3

and,

A - 5 = 4 × (B - 5)

A - 5 = 4B - 20

4B = A - 5 + 20

4B = A + 15

By substituting above equation,

{4over3}A = A + 15 

{4over3}A - A = 15

{{4A -3 A}over3} = 15

A = 15 × 3

A = 45

Hence, Rohit's present age is **45 years.**

questions.question: The total of the ages of Ram, Shyam and Adil is 60 years. What was the total of their ages four years ago ?
questions.solution:
Ram + Shyam + Adil = 60 years

Four years ago each of them was 4 years younger.

So, total of their ages four years ago = [60 – (3 × 4)] years

= 60 – 12

= 48 years

Hence, ’48 years’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: Raman's age is twice to the age of his daughter Shruti. If ten years ago Raman's age was three times to the age of Shruti, then what is the present age of Shruti?
questions.solution:
Let Shruti's age is ‘x’ years.

So, Raman’s age = 2x years

Age of Raman ten years ago was (2x – 10) years and that of Shruti was (x – 10) years.

According to question:

2x – 10 = 3(x – 10)

=> 2x – 10 = 3x – 30

=> 2x – 3x = -30 + 10

=> -x = - 20

=> x = 20

So, present age of Shruti is 20 years.

Hence, ‘**20 years**’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: Three persons A, B and C had Rs. 360 altogether. A transferred half of the amount he had to B and C transferred half of the amount he had to A. After the transfer, all of them have equal amounts. What is the total amount B had before the transfer?
questions.solution:
Given,

Three persons A, B, and C had Rs. 360 altogether.

A transferred half of the amount he had to B and C transferred half of the amount he had to A.

After the transfer, all of them have equal amounts.

Therefore, A + B + C = 360 at the end they have 120 each.

Final amount of A = Final amount of B = Final amount of C = 120

Let 2y be the initial amount with C.

Then amount given by C to A = y

Final amount of C = 120 = inital amount of C - amount transferred to A = 2y - y = y

Therefore, y = 120.

Therefore, initial amount of C must be 240 and amount transferred to A = 120.

So, initially, A + B = 120 because A + B + C = 360.

Now, final amount of B = 120 and before transfer A + B = 120........ (I)

**Let 2x be the amount with A initially and z be the initial amount with B.**

Then 2x + z = 120. (from I) ..........(1)

Also, x + z = 120 (amount transferred by A + initial amount of B = final amount of B) .............(2)

From (1) and (2), we get 2x + z = x + z.

⇒ 2x = x

⇒ x = 0 and z = 120.

Hence, B had Rs. 120 initially.

questions.question: The District Transport Authority has started special bus services for college going students. One bus starts from village P. The number of girls in the bus is one-fourth of the number of boys. In village Q, 20 boys leave the bus at their college stop and ten girls enter the bus. Now the number of boys and girls is equal. How many students enter the bus in the beginning?
questions.solution:
Let,

**Number of girls = G**

**Number of boys = B**

**At village P

Number of girls in the bus is one-fourth of the number of boys so,

=> G = 1/4B

=> 4G = B

At village Q**

20 boys leave the bus at their college stop and ten girls enter the bus.

Number of girls = G + 10

Number of boys = B - 20

Now the number of boys and girls is equal

=> G + 10 = B – 20

∵ 4G = B

So,

=> G + 10 = 4G – 20

=> 4G - 4 = 20 + 10

=> 3G = 30

=> G = 10

∵ 4G = B

So, B = 4 × 10

B = 40

Total number of students enter the bus in the beginning = B + G = 10 + 40 = 50

Hence, Total number of students enter the bus in the beginning is **“50”**.

questions.question: Kritika had ₹21,450 with her. She spent 16% of this amount on conveyance. Then, she spent 50% of the remaining amount on ration. Then, she spent ₹991 on internet expenses. How many rupees is left with her now?
questions.solution:
Amount of money Kritika had = ₹21,450

Percentage of money she spent on conveyance = 16%

Amount of money she spent on conveyance = 16/100 × ₹21,450 = ₹3,432

Amount of money left with Kritika = ₹ (21,450 – 3,432) = ₹18,018

Then, she spent 50% of the remaining amount on ration.

Amount of money spent on ration = 50/100 × ₹18,018 = ₹9,009

Amount of money left with Kritika = ₹(18,018 - 9,009) = ₹9,009

Then, she spent ₹991 on internet expenses.

Therefore, amount of money left with her now = ₹ (9,009 – 991) = ₹8,018

Hence, ‘**₹8,018**’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: In an entrance test, Tiwari scored 25% marks and failed by 64 marks. If he had scored 40% marks, then he would have secured 32 marks more than the pass marks. Find the pass marks.
questions.solution:
**Let,**

**X is the passing mark**

**Y is the total marks.**

**Given:**

**1) **Tiwari scored 25% marks and failed by 64 marks.

X – 64 = 25%Y **-------- eq. (1)**

2) He had scored 40% marks, then he would have secured 32 marks more than the pass marks.

X + 32 = 40%Y **-------- eq. (2)**

**Subtract eq. (2) from eq. (1)**

=> (X + 32) – (X – 64) = 40%Y - 25%Y

=> 32 + 64 = 15%Y

=> 96 = 15%Y

=> Y = 96 ÷ (15/100)</p&

questions.question: The sum of the ages of 4 friends A, B, C and D is 70 years. What would be the total of their ages 5 years later?
questions.solution:
The sum of the ages of 4 friends A, B, C and D is 70 years.

A + B + C + D = 70 years

The total of their ages after 5 years will increase by 20 years as 5 × 4 = 20.

So, total age of 4 friends after 5 years = (70 + 20) years

= 90 years

Hence, **90 **is the correct answer.
